claims.statement: The instructions-in-use fragment describes saved files as available and automatically included in submitted requests. Its Yes/No feedback links ask whether a file was added; neither a feedback click nor file existence certifies supported scope, prompt inclusion or effective behavior. No feedback was submitted.
The organization-support note confines support at the pin to website chat, website code review and website cloud agent. Organization instructions cannot be assumed supported in every IDE or CLI.

The path procedure requires files ending .instructions.md under .github/instructions or descendants and applyTo glob metadata. Comma-separated patterns include both ts and tsx in its TypeScript example; examples are scope selectors, not enforced file-access restrictions.

The glob examples distinguish current-directory matching from recursive matching, including src/*.py excluding nested paths versus src/**/*.py including them. The any-depth subdir example requires that directory segment; matching Python files outside such a segment is not implied.

The excludeAgent metadata accepts code-review or cloud-agent to exclude that named consumer; the all-files example excludes review and describes cloud-agent use. With no exclusion it describes both consumers using instructions, subject to product support and configuration rather than guaranteed runtime loading.
The procedure permits natural-language Markdown with flexible whitespace/paragraph layout. Formatting or valid glob metadata does not guarantee safe, unambiguous or consistently obeyed instructions.

The reference fragment says a response References entry for .github/copilot-instructions.md indicates it was included in the model prompt, even when instructions are not shown in chat/inline chat. Such an entry is inclusion evidence, not proof the model obeyed it; no target reference entry observed.
The nondeterminism note explicitly warns instructions may not be followed the same way each time. Instruction loading cannot substitute for behavioral enforcement or repeated negative-case tests.

The customization note calls examples inspiration, links community material and makes instruction scope depend on platform or IDE. It is not adoption, universal support or an assurance of third-party rights.
